title: Notification Center
prompt: Design an in-app notification drawer with unread count, paged history and mark-as-read. Browser push is optional and separate. Events may be duplicated, multiple tabs may be open and the drawer should remain usable if the live connection fails. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Fetch unread count and paginated history
Mark individual/all notifications read and reconcile count
Apply live events without duplicating rows or losing focus
nonFunctionalReqs: 100 notifications per retained page window; bursty live events; coalesce badge updates without blocking drawer controls.
Use a labelled drawer/dialog with appropriate focus management and Escape behavior; return focus to bell on close. Announce a concise count change, not every historical row.
Read mutation is idempotent; accept only current count versions and refresh authoritative state after a gap. Broadcast invalidation across tabs if supported.

scale.notes: 100 notifications per retained page window; bursty live events; coalesce badge updates without blocking drawer controls.
scale.storage: 50 duplicate events for 1 notification; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Use a versioned unread-count snapshot and ID-based notification deduplication. Optimistic read state is a reversible overlay until acknowledgement. After connection gaps refetch count and page before accepting later events.
Two tabs read the same notification during a reconnect
Periodic polling may be sufficient. SSE fits server-to-client deltas; WebSocket is useful only when bidirectional traffic is needed.
